video.title: Forget Dropshipping. This Side Hustle Is 10x Easier (and Smarter)

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Cody Schneider about AI-powered Etsy print-on-demand: use Everbe to find best-selling Etsy products, generate similar vector graphics with the ChatGPT image API, automate the pipeline with n8n (workflow JSON written by Claude/Perplexity), push to Printify and publish to Etsy for a volume game of thousands of listings. They also cover Google Shopping ads arbitrage, a comparison with dropshipping, other POD/digital product categories, and a pitch to build merch stores for creators on a 5% revenue share via cold email. Key takeaway: AI image generation removes the design bottleneck, but results are unproven and the numbers are speculative.

speakers.description: Marketer and entrepreneur with 10+ years selling on Etsy; idea guy on AI and growth

ideas.name: AI-generated Etsy print-on-demand at scale
ideas.one_liner: Find best-selling Etsy products, generate similar AI graphics, and auto-publish thousands of print-on-demand listings via Printify to Etsy.
ideas.business_model: One-off product sales via Etsy marketplace; print-on-demand supplier fulfils; margin is sale price minus production cost, Etsy fees and listing fees.
ideas.customer: Etsy shoppers searching for niche graphic apparel and gifts (e.g. horse sweatshirts).
ideas.problem: Creating large catalogues of designs used to need design skills or offshore illustrators; finding what sells is guesswork.
ideas.offer: Graphic apparel and merchandise (shirts, sweatshirts, mugs, stickers) with designs modelled on proven best sellers.

pricing.model: Copy the pricing structure of the winning listings
pricing.notes: Exact prices not stated; Etsy listing fee mentioned as roughly 20 or 30 cents.

acquisition_channels.details: Rank in Etsy internal search using the same keywords in title and description as the winning listings; Etsy supplies the traffic and trust ('parasite SEO').

quote.text: you're using the domain authority and the the current rankings of these websites to get like sales
quote.speaker: Cody Schneider

acquisition_channels.details: Etsy category pages rank on Google for generic keywords, so listings benefit from that traffic.

ideas.delivery: Printify prints and ships from its factories; pipeline: scrape winners, generate image via ChatGPT image API, remove background, upload to Printify, bulk publish to Etsy. Research and final publish are the only manual steps, though even those could be automated.
unit_economics_claims: Costs are Everbe subscription, image generation cost and Etsy listing fee
Roughly 20% of products make 80% of revenue
ideas.startup_cost: Basically zero; a weekend of about 8 hours to learn

acquisition.how: Inbound marketplace search; agents can generate and optimise listings, with occasional human review.

onboarding.how: No customer onboarding; buyers check out on Etsy.

delivery.how: Printify handles production and shipping; the image pipeline is automatable, with human checks for trademark and quality.

support.how: Order issues and messages could be agent-handled, but refunds and disputes need a human sometimes.

uk_applicability.notes: Etsy, Printify and Printful all operate in the UK, with UK production options; need to handle VAT, UK trademark and IP rules, and Etsy policies on AI and copying listings.

risks: Copying best-selling listings invites IP and copyright complaints
Trademark takedowns on phrases can lead to shop suspension after about three strikes
Etsy may restrict mass AI-generated listings
Most listings will not sell and results are unproven
Market saturation as more people copy the method

ideas.name: Merch store builder for creators on revenue share
ideas.one_liner: Cold email creators with 'I built you a merch store', build it if they say yes, and take 5% of revenue.
ideas.business_model: Revenue share of 5% of merch sales, no upfront fee
ideas.customer: Content creators, especially long-form YouTubers and podcasters with large audiences who do not yet sell merch
ideas.problem: Most creators do not sell merch because of the hassle of design, store setup and logistics
ideas.offer: A fully built, managed merch store with designs based on the creator's catchphrases, run on Fourthwall or similar

acquisition_channels.details: Scrape creator emails with Apify YouTube email scraper, validate with MillionVerifier, send via Instantly with subject line 'I built you a merch store'. If they reply yes, build and send the store.

quote.text: Cold email is I built you a merch store. All lowercase. That's the subject line.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: DM creators on Instagram as an alternative.

ideas.delivery: Analyse transcripts for recurring catchphrases, design merch around them, set up a store on Fourthwall or Shopify with a cheap domain, and manage designs and logistics. Print-on-demand partner handles production and shipping.
unit_economics_claims: Ten creators could reach about a quarter million a year (hypothetical)
ideas.startup_cost: About $10 domain and Shopify free trial for 30 days

acquisition.how: Cold email to creators can be automated, but many are individuals or sole traders, so UK PECR consent rules limit this.

onboarding.how: Agents can build store drafts and contracts; a human approves.

delivery.how: Agents analyse transcripts, generate designs and list products; print partner ships.

billing.how: Platform handles payouts; revenue share reconciliation needs checks.

support.how: Creator relationship needs occasional human contact.

uk_applicability.notes: Cold email to sole-trader creators breaches PECR without consent; limited-company creators are fine. Instagram DMs are also restricted. Fourthwall operates in the UK.

lessons.lesson: Use data tools to find proven demand rather than guessing, then copy the pattern.
Volume strategies expect a power-law outcome: a small share of listings drive most revenue, so surface area matters.
AI removes the human labour bottleneck in creative production, which was previously the moat.
LLMs can write automation workflow files, making complex tools like n8n usable by non-coders.
Print-on-demand carries no inventory or sunk cost, which makes it a better business model than dropshipping and possible to sell.
Pitch with finished examples, such as a built store, rather than abstract proposals; it makes the offer easy to say yes to.
A first business is mostly for acquiring skills; downside is small and the learning compounds into the next venture.

quote.text: worst case, you make no money, but you learn.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Do not get stuck on one product type; stickers, mugs, notebooks and digital goods can have better margins than apparel.
Thin-margin ad arbitrage can be amplified by credit-card rewards on ad spend, but only if volume is large.

evidence_quality.rationale: Cody describes a method and past Etsy experience but gives no concrete revenue or results for the AI version; income figures are hypothetical and the creator-merch idea is brainstormed live. Little verification of Etsy policy on mass AI listings.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris promotes his TKOwners paid community and newsletter/podcast; Cody has a friend who owns Everbe, which he recommends.
